# Regression QA - RC 2.14: transaction-categorization findings

**Test round:** RC 2.14 pre-release categorization pass
**Prepared by:** QA (enrichment)
**Verdict:** Not signed off - the findings below must clear before this build ships

## Summary

The RC 2.14 pass replays our labelled statement-fixture corpus through the
enrichment stage and diffs every derived field against the accepted baseline.
The overwhelming majority of fixtures reproduce their baseline labels exactly.
A thin residue of rows, though, now derive a category or a counterparty name
that disagrees with the accepted answer. Each regressed row is stable - the same
fixture yields the identical wrong field every time it is replayed - and each one
hinges on a narrow, individually rare pattern in the underlying reference text
rather than on the size of the amount or on which customer it belongs to.
Ordinary purchases, routine transfers and everyday deposits all reproduce
baseline, which is why the aggregate diff read clean until these edge fixtures
were isolated.

The findings are recorded in the order they surfaced. QA has not traced any of
them to a root cause; that is left to engineering. Acceptance for this build is
simply that every listed finding derives its baseline field again and that no
fixture already matching baseline moves.

## Findings

**F-1.** A cheque-type debit whose statement note carries nothing but the
instrument's own number - a short, bare run of digits with no other text sitting
beside it - is landing in the generic transfer bucket. Cheque debits whose notes
are shaped even slightly differently keep their correct cheque label, so the miss
is confined to this one bare-number note form.

**F-2.** On a cleared cheque, the counterparty column is coming back with an
internal clearing tag in place of the account-holder's name. The affected rows
all share one raw-narration layout, copied here from a fixture:

> `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR`

For this layout the field is returning a fragment of the reference instead of the
name that should be lifted from it.

**F-3.** A slice of inbound electronic-transfer credits - the plain
national-transfer kind - are arriving with the counterparty-name column left
completely blank. The category on these rows is right; it is only the name that
goes missing. Other electronic-transfer credits, whose references are laid out
differently, still resolve their names normally, so this is not a blanket failure
of name extraction.

**F-4.** An incoming person-to-person instant-payment credit is showing a bare
reference number where the sender's name belongs. The value that surfaces is a
fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from;
neighbouring instant-payment layouts still resolve their names correctly.

**F-5.** A small nominal deposit that a bank posts purely to confirm an account
is reachable - the token "is this account live" credit rather than a real
payment - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being recognised as
an account-verification entry. Ordinary deposits are untouched; only these token
confirmation credits regressed.

## Exit criteria

The enrichment path is fully deterministic and runs offline, so each finding
above is reproducible on demand from the fixture that triggered it. Restore the
correct category and counterparty on the listed forms without disturbing any
fixture that already agrees with baseline. A change that rescues these rows but
shifts the label or the name of ordinary, currently-correct traffic does not meet
acceptance: the bar is that the specific regressions listed here clear and
everything else stays exactly where the baseline has it.

# Research Report: Transaction Categorization / Enrichment Repo at /app

## 1. Overall Repo Structure

Single-commit git repo (`047782b import codebase`) containing a **Python 3.9 Flask microservice** ("categorizationapp", internally called `transaction-enrichment-python` per the Dockerfile) that enriches Indian bank statement transactions using **pandas + numpy vectorized regex rules** (no ML; scikit-learn is a declared dep but the core logic is `np.select` over regex conditions).

```
/app
├── .gitignore
├── Dockerfile                          # python:3.9.2, pip install -e ., gunicorn on :9898
└── categorizationapp/
    ├── setup.py                        # deps: Flask 1.1.2, pandas 1.2.4, fuzzywuzzy, python-Levenshtein, gunicorn...
    └── categorizationapp/
        ├── __init__.py                 # Flask app factory + request timing logging
        ├── Controller.py               # HTTP routes; per-bank dispatch (936 lines, heavily duplicated)
        ├── BankScripts/                # 33 per-bank categorizers (HDFC, SBI, ICICI, Axis, Kotak, ...)
        └── UtilityScripts/
            ├── AppUtil.py              # sep_by_* splitters, py_extract, fuzzy_match
            ├── RegexConstants.py       # cross-bank semantic regexes (SALARY, LOAN, INSURANCE, ...)
            ├── BankRegexConstants.py   # bank-specific narration patterns (CHQ/NEFT/IMPS/FT patterns)
            ├── Purpose.py              # transactionSubcategory assignment (savings/current)
            ├── CleanName.py            # partyName -> canonical merchant name (1971 lines)
            ├── CardCleanNames.py       # same for credit-card txns
            ├── CardPurpose.py          # subcategory for credit-card txns
            ├── InternalPayment.py      # self-transfer detection via fuzzy name match
            ├── SalaryDetection.py      # recurring-credit clustering salary detector
            ├── PFMCategorization.py    # PFM roll-up categories
            ├── SimpleDescription.py    # human-readable description
            ├── RecurrentTxns.py        # recurring txn detection
            ├── TransactionCategoryEnums.py / TransactionSubcategoryEnums.py
```

**Build/run**: `pip3 install -e .` inside `/app/categorizationapp`, then `gunicorn -w 4 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app` (see `/app/Dockerfile`). Endpoints: `POST /categorizeTransaction` (payload: `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder`, `isPFMEnabled`, `transactions[]`) and `POST /recurrentTransactions` (`/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py:69` and `:55`).

## 2. Where Enrichment/Categorization Logic Lives

Pipeline per request (Controller.py, e.g. HDFC branch lines 163–186; identical blocks repeat per bank):
1. `AppUtil.clean_input_df` (Controller.py:87) — normalizes `description`, `amount`, `balanceAfterTransaction`.
2. `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` in `BankScripts/<Bank>.py` — sets **`transactionCategory`** (default `"TRANSFER"`), **`transactionSubcategory`**, **`merchantType`**, and raw **`partyName`** (counterparty) + `party2` (whitespace-stripped copy).
3. `purpose()` — `/app/.../UtilityScripts/Purpose.py:9` — refines `transactionSubcategory` (SALARY, LOAN_REPAYMENT, INSURANCE, FUEL, TRAVEL, etc.) using regex constants from `RegexConstants.py`.
4. `clean_names()` — `/app/.../UtilityScripts/CleanName.py:9` — maps raw partyName/description to canonical merchant names ("TataSky DTH", "BESCOM"...).
5. `internal_payment()` — `/app/.../UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py:8` — fuzzywuzzy match of partyName vs. accountHolder (ratio > 75) to mark `INTERNAL_PAYMENT` / `isInternalPayment`.
6. `salary_detection()` (SalaryDetection.py), and optionally `pfm_categorization()` (PFMCategorization.py:8) + `simple_description()`.

**Category derivation mechanics** (each bank script): a list of `[boolean-Series condition, "CATEGORY"]` pairs evaluated by `np.select`, first match wins. Example: `categorize_HDFC_transactions` — `/app/.../BankScripts/HDFC.py:9`, categories at lines 11–104; partyName extraction at lines 146–275. `categorize_SBI_transactions` — `/app/.../BankScripts/SBI.py:8`, categories at 10–70, partyName at 97–192.

**Counterparty extraction helpers** — `/app/.../UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py`:
- `sep_by_(desc,n1,n2)` (line 14, split on `/`), `sep_by_dash` (17), `sep_by_colon` (29), `sep_by_star` (23), `sep_by_wave/comma/under/...` — positional token extraction.
- `py_extract(desc, pat, index)` (line 61) — case-insensitive `str.extract` with NaN→"" handling.
- `fuzzy_match` (line 48) — fuzzywuzzy ratio.

## 3. Cheque Transaction Categorization (CHQ / cheque / MICR CLG)

Categories produced: `CHEQUE_PAID`, `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT`, `CHEQUE_RETURN`, `CHEQUE_RETURN_PENALTY`, `CHEQUE_CASH_WITHDRAWAL`, `STOP_CHEQUE_CHARGES`, `INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE`.

Key sites (all condition regexes are `description.str.contains(..., case=False)` gated on DEBIT/CREDIT):

- **HDFC** (`BankScripts/HDFC.py`):
  - line 71 DEBIT / line 73 CREDIT: `"\\b[Cc][Hh][Qq]\\b|^I/W CHQ RETURN|[Cc]heque|CHEQUE"` → CHEQUE_PAID / CHEQUE_DEPOSIT
  - lines 69–70, 72: returns (`^I/W CHQ RET|CHQ DEP RET|MC CANCELLED|CHQ RTN`, `REVERSAL.*CLG`)
  - line 30: penalty (`CHQ RETURN CHG|CHQ DEP RET CHG|Chq RTN C\s?ha?rg|GST.*Chq rtn`)
  - line 100: 16-char remark `^[0]{11}[0-9]{5}` on CREDIT → CHEQUE_DEPOSIT
  - line 126: CHEQUE_PAID followed by CHEQUE_RETURN with negative balance → INSUFFICIENTS_FUNDS_BOUNCE
  - Cheque **partyName** (lines 188–197) via `HDFC_CHQ_PATTERN1..10` in `BankRegexConstants.py:81-90`, notably MICR clearing forms: `"MICR 1 CLG - NO :|- - MICR CLG -|- MICR - MICR CLG -|MICR 8 CLEARI :|-TOW : |-WBO:|-PUNE:"` (PATTERN1), `"CHQ DEP - MICR [0-9] CLEARING|MICR CLG - [A-Z]+ : "` (PATTERN2), `"^[0-9]+(.*) - CHQ PAI\s?D -"` (PATTERN7), `"CHQ DEP - .* - MICR.*:(.*):"` (PATTERN10). Name is pulled by `sep_by_colon`/`sep_by_dash`/`py_extract`. MICR junk is nulled at line 260 (`partyName contains "Micr Clg|Chq Paid"` → "").
- **SBI** (`BankScripts/SBI.py:45-47`): `"\\bCLG\\b|^BY CLEARING|^TO CLEARING|\\bCHQ\\b|CHEQUE|CHEQ NO"` DEBIT→CHEQUE_PAID, CREDIT→CHEQUE_DEPOSIT; `\bCH [0-9]{6}-` CREDIT→CHEQUE_DEPOSIT; partyName at line 123 for `^CASH CHEQUE-|^CHEQUE DEPOSIT-|^CHEQUE WDL- `.
- **Kotak** (`BankScripts/Kotak.py:64,66`): `"\\bCLG\\b|\\bMICR\\b|\\bCHQ\\b|^BY INST |^TRF CHQ[0-9]"`; MICR-inward partyName via `CHQ_PATTERN1..4` (`BankRegexConstants.py:314-317`, e.g. `"MICR INWARD.*TO CLG (.*)"`) at Kotak.py:235-238, then bank-name suffixes removed with `CHQ_CLEAN_KOTAK` (BankRegexConstants.py:318).
- **ICICI** (`BankScripts/ICICI.py:69-72`): `\bC[Ll][Gg]\b|INWARD CLEARING` and remark contains `CHEQUE`; extraction `^CLG/(?!(CHQ|CLG))` at line 161.
- Others: YES.py:45-46 (`CHQ DEP|CHEQUE DEPOSIT|CHQ PAID|CHQNO|^IP CHQ|^OS CHQ` / `^CTS CLG|...`), UnionBank.py:50-51 (`\bmicr.*clg|\bcts.*clg|^By\b`), StandardCharted.py:43-45 + 146-148 (`INWARD CLG CHQ WITHDRAWAL [0-9]{6} (.*)`), IDBI.py:55-58, Federal.py:41-42 (`^CLG/`), CityUnion.py:41-42 & 77-134 (`TO CHQ TRANSFER:...` colon-token extraction), PNB cheque partyName patterns `PNB_CHQ_0..8` (BankRegexConstants.py:140-148), UCO `UCO_CHQ_PATTERN1..4` (BankRegexConstants.py:380-383), BOM cheque cleaners `CHQ_CLEAN/CHQ_CLEAN2` (BankRegexConstants.py:361-362). Several banks also infer cheques from the **remark** field being a 3-6 digit cheque number (YES.py:52-53, UCO.py:44-45, TamilnadMerchantile.py:33-34, SouthIndian.py:32).
- Kotak funds-transfer-by-cheque: `FT_CHQ_PATTERN1..37` (`BankRegexConstants.py:263-299`, e.g. `"^TRF FROM CHQ [0-9]+ (.*)"`, `"^BY INST [0-9]+ TRANSFER FRM (.*)"`) applied at Kotak.py:190-226.

## 4. NEFT / IMPS / UPI / RTGS Counterparty Extraction

Category detection first (per bank), then positional/regex name extraction. Representative patterns:

- **HDFC** (`HDFC.py`): detection lines 57-62 (`-TPT-`→TPT, `^UPI|UPI-?\s?`→UPI, `IMPS-`→IMPS, `NEFT [CcDd][Rr]-|[0-9]NEFT TO|^BULK NEFT`→NEFT, `RTGS`→RTGS). Extraction:
  - UPI: line 154 `^UPI-` → `sep_by_dash(desc,1,2)` (2nd dash token = payee name); special cases for BILLDESK (149), Razorpay handles `-RZ?PY\.(.*)@` (153), PAYTM (228-229), numeric-name fallback to token 2-3 (227).
  - NEFT: line 157 `^NEFT [CD][Rr]-[A-z0-9]{11}-[0-9]{7,}-` → dash tokens 3-4; line 158 `...-[A-Z]-` → tokens 2-4; generic `^IMPS-|^NEFT [CD][Rr]` → tokens 2-3 (159); `^00[0-9]+NEFT TO ` → `py_extract("NEFT TO (.*)")` (161).
  - IMPS: Razorpay merchant forms at 155-156 (tokens 6-7 / 5-6); generic token 2-3 (159); `^IMPS.*-UNREGISTERED-` → token 4-5 (251).
  - RTGS/INTERNET_BANKING fallback: category in {NEFT,RTGS,IMPS,INTERNET_BANKING} → dash tokens 2-3 (162).
- **SBI** (`SBI.py`): UPI = slash token 3-4 (line 99, format `TO TRANSFER-UPI/DR/<ref>/<name>/...`); NEFT = star token 3-4 with digit/punct strip (122) or INB-NEFT dash tokens (120-121); RTGS via `py_extract("NO:\s[A-Z0-9]+(.*)")` (119); IMPS via `SBI_IMPS_1..3` (BankRegexConstants.py:60-62, e.g. `^BY TRANSFER-INB IMPS.*XX0[0-9]{3}/[A-Za-z]`) → slash token 3-4 (149-151).
- **Kotak** (`Kotak.py:109-116, 144-154`): uses shared constants in `BankRegexConstants.py`:
  - IMPS: `IMPS_PATTERN1..8` (lines 195-202), e.g. `"^IMPS from (.*)Ref"`, `"IB IMPS TO (.*) Ref"`; also `RCVD_FROM_IMPS1..5` (lines 234-238), `"^Received from (.*) IMPS REF"` (Kotak.py:243-247).
  - NEFT: `NEFT_PATTERN0..7` (lines 206-213), e.g. `"^NEFT [0-9]+1DC (.*) [A-Z]{4}[0-9]"`, `"NEFT AXISCN[0-9]+ (.*)"`, `"(NEFT [A-Z]{3,5}|...)[0-9]+(.*)"`; trailing bank/IFSC noise removed with `NEFT_CLEAN_KOTAK` (line 214).
  - RTGS: `KT_RTGS_PATTERN = "RTGS [A-Z]{3,5}[0-9]+ (.*)"`, `RTGS_PATTERN1 = "^IB:RTGS (.*)"` (lines 217-218).
- **Union Bank** (`UnionBank.py:81-105`): `UB_NEFT_1..8` (`BankRegexConstants.py:120-127`, e.g. `"^NEFT:IBUSER-(.*) SAA[0-9]+"`, `"NEFT fm (.*):\s?SAA"`), `UB_RTGS_1/2` (`"RTGS:[0-9]+(.*) [A-Z]{4}[0-9]{12}"`); UPI `^UPI-`→dash 1-2 or slash 3-4; IMPS `^IMPS/`→slash 3-4.
- **YES** (`YES.py:96-112`): UPI `^UPI/[0-9]+/From:` → `From:(.*)/To` (credit) or `/To:(.*)/`(debit); NEFT `NEFT [CD][Rr] -` dash 2-3, `^NEFT O/W [NP]` → `" /W [NP][0-9]{15} (.*)"`; RTGS `^RTGS [CD][Rr]-` dash 2-3.
- **ICICI** (`ICICI.py:139`): UPI → slash tokens 3-4 (format `UPI/<ref>/<remark>/<name>/...`); Razorpay override to token 2-3 at line 211.
- **IDFC** (`IDFC.py:71-85`): IMPS `IMPS-INET|MOB|RIB/` → slash 3-4; `^NEFT/` and `RTGS/` → slash 2-3; `^UPI/MOB/` → slash 3-4; junk removed via `UPI_CLEAN` (line 66).
- Others follow the same template: PNB (`^UPI/.*P2M`→slash 3-4, P2A→4-5; RTGS keyword list `PNB_RTGS_KEYWORDS` BankRegexConstants.py:151), UCO (`MPAYUPITRTR...` extracts at UCO.py:71-77), StandardCharted (UPI slash-position variants at 113-117), Federal, RBL, DCB, TamilnadMerchantile (`IMPS by (.*)`), SouthIndian (`UPI/YESB/` token counting).

Post-processing everywhere: `.str.title()`, junk stripping (`^Na$|^Upi$|Razorpay|Unregistered...`), location/bank-name removal (`LOCATION_CLEAN` BankRegexConstants.py:64, `TRF_STOP_WORDS` line 65, `REMOVE_BANK_CB` line 417), duplicate-row reversal heuristic (consecutive DEBIT/CREDIT same amount+description containing `IMPS|NEFT|\bUPI|RTGS` → REVERSAL, e.g. HDFC.py:98, ICICI.py:49, Saraswat.py:20).

## 5. Test Fixtures and Test Commands

**There are none.** Findings:
- Complete file inventory (52 tracked files) contains no `tests/` directory, no `test_*.py`, no pytest/unittest/tox/CI config, no labelled statement fixtures, and no baseline files. Searches for `test|pytest|unittest|fixture|baseline` only hit incidental strings (a `# For testing purpose only` comment in `SalaryDetection.py:27` and `RecurrentTxns.py:16`, and "TEST*.xml" in `.gitignore:30` — a leftover from a generic template).
- `.gitignore` ignores `*.csv`, suggesting fixture CSVs may have existed locally but were never committed.
- Therefore the only way to exercise the code is running the service: `cd /app/categorizationapp && pip install -e . && gunicorn -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app` (or `docker build`), then POSTing JSON to `/categorizeTransaction`. There is no automated test command in the repo.

### Key file/line quick reference
| Concern | Location |
|---|---|
| HTTP routes / per-bank dispatch | `Controller.py:55, 69, 91-936` |
| Category derivation (per bank) | `BankScripts/<Bank>.py` first `conditions_choices` block (e.g. HDFC.py:11-104, SBI.py:10-70, ICICI.py, Kotak.py) |
| Counterparty (partyName) extraction | same files, later blocks (HDFC.py:146-275, SBI.py:97-192, Kotak.py:109-247) |
| Shared cheque/NEFT/IMPS/RTGS/FT regex constants | `UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py` (CHQ: 81-90, 140-148, 263-318, 380-383; IMPS: 195-202, 234-238; NEFT: 206-214; RTGS: 217-218, 128-129, 151) |
| Semantic category regexes (salary/loan/insurance/...) | `UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py:5-190` |
| Splitter/extractor utilities | `UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py:14-66` |
| Subcategory ("purpose") | `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py:9` |
| Merchant name canonicalization | `UtilityScripts/CleanName.py:9`, `CardCleanNames.py` |
| Internal-payment detection | `UtilityScripts/InternalPayment.py:8` |
| PFM roll-up | `UtilityScripts/PFMCategorization.py:8` |
</task_result>

57:     @params description => input string


**Why it's wrong (off-by-one grabbing the reference token):**
- The standard inbound IMPS P2A/P2P credit narration is `IMPS/P2A/<12-digit ref>/<SENDER NAME>/<bank>/<remark>`. Split on `/`: token 0 = `IMPS`, token 1 = `P2A` (mode), **token 2 = the numeric reference**, token 3 = the sender's name. `sep_by_(description, 2, 3)` therefore surfaces the bare 12-digit reference number — exactly "a fragment of the very reference string the name should have been read from."
- **Sibling rules in the same script are consistent/correct for the identical `keyword/mode/ref/name` family:** the UPI rules on lines 59–60 (`UPI/CR/<ref>/<name>`, `UPI/REV/<ref>/<name>`) correctly skip the numeric ref and take token **3,4**. The IMPS rule alone is one index short. Line 62 (NEFT/RTGS) using 2,3 is fine because NEFT narrations lack the mode token (`NEFT/<UTR>/<name>` → token 2 is the name).
- Cross-bank corroboration for this narration family in this codebase: UCO.py:69 (`^IMPS/P2A/` → `sep_by_(...,3,4)`), Andhra.py:69 (`^IMPS/` → 3,4), BOB.py:135 (`IMPS/P2A/` → 3,4), Indusind (uses 4,5 for its longer layout). Bandhan's `2,3` is the outlier.

**Why the buggy value survives (crucial per your criteria):**
- Bandhan.py has **no cleanup pass at all** on `partyName` after the `np.select` — lines 71–76 are only:
```python
72: transactions['partyName'] = np.select(df['conditions'], df['choices'], default="")
74: transactions['partyName'] = transactions['partyName'].str.strip().str.title()
76: transactions['party2'] = transactions['partyName'].replace(to_replace=" ", value="", regex=True)
```
  There is no `^[0-9]{4,}$` / `[0-9]{5,}` blanking rule anywhere in the script, and `.str.title()` leaves digits unchanged. A pure-numeric reference token surfaces verbatim to the caller.
- `np.select` is first-match-wins: no later rule can override the IMPS row, since 59/60 (UPI) precede it and nothing after it matches IMPS.

**Correct fix:** line 61 should be `sep_by_(transactions.description, 3, 4)` for the `IMPS/P2A/...` layout (i.e., consistent with the UPI siblings on lines 59–60), ideally conditioned like the UPI rules, e.g. `IMPS/(P2[AP]|[CD]R)/[0-9]+/`.

F-1: PNB debit bare 6-digit cheque remark -> CHEQUE_PAID (PNB.py:60)
F-2: Canara 'CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-<name>' -> extract name not clearing tag (Canara.py:165)
F-3: PNB '^NEFT ' credit blank partyName (PNB.py:110 index=1)
F-4: Bandhan IMPS P2A credit shows ref number (Bandhan.py:61)
F-5: Canara Rs.1 penny-drop -> ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION (Canara.py:19 lt(1))
Re-run harness post-fix + no-regression spot checks

steps.message:
All five findings traced to root cause, fixed, and verified. Summary of the diagnosis and the surgical fixes:

**F-1 — bare cheque-number debit → TRANSFER** (`BankScripts/PNB.py:60`)
The debit-side rule that classifies a transaction as a cheque from a digits-only remark accepted only exactly 5 digits (`^[0-9]{5}$`), while its credit-side twin one line below accepts `^[0-9]{5,6}$`. Standard 6-digit cheque numbers on debits fell through to the `TRANSFER` default. Fixed to `^[0-9]{5,6}$`, symmetric with the credit rule.

**F-2 — `CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-RAVI KUMAR` returns "Micr Clg"** (`BankScripts/Canara.py`)
The generic `^CHQ PAID-` extractor takes dash-token 1, which for the MICR-clearing layout is the clearing tag, not the name (token 2). The sibling rule for `Chq Paid-Home Clearing-` already correctly takes token 2. Added a dedicated `^CHQ PAID-MICR CLG-` rule taking token 2,3 ahead of the generic rule — single-dash `CHQ PAID-<name>` narrations (currently correct via token 1) are untouched.

**F-3 — plain NEFT credits with blank counterparty** (`BankScripts/PNB.py:110`)
The `^NEFT ` layout used `py_extract(..., pat="NEFT (.*)", index=1)` — the pattern has only one capture group, so group index 1 doesn't exist and `py_extract` returns empty for every matching row. All other calls in the codebase use `index=0` for single-group patterns. Fixed to `index=0`.

**F-4 — inbound IMPS P2P credit shows the reference number** (`BankScripts/Bandhan.py:61`)
For `IMPS/P2A/<ref>/<SENDER>/...` layouts the rule took slash-token 2 (the numeric reference) instead of token 3 (the sender). The adjacent UPI rules for the identical `scheme/mode/ref/name` shape correctly use 3,4, and Bandhan has no downstream cleanup that blanks numerics — hence the bare ref surfaced. Added a mode-token rule (`IMPS/(P2A|P2P|CR|DR)/`) taking token 3,4 before the generic rule, so mode-less `IMPS/<ref>/<name>` layouts keep deriving exactly as they do today.

**F-5 — ₹1 penny-drop credit filed as TRANSFER** (`BankScripts/Canara.py:19`)
The verification rule required `amount.lt(1)`, which excludes the canonical ₹1 confirmation credit. Every other bank uses `eq(1)`, `isin([1,-1])`, or `lt(2)` (HDFC/PNB use the identical `lt(2)` structure). Fixed to `amount.lt(2)`; sub-rupee rows are unaffected (still match), ordinary deposits ≥ ₹2 are unaffected.

Verification: I built a harness (`/tmp/opencode/repro.py`) reproducing each finding on the pre-fix code, plus a 59-narration differential battery (`/tmp/opencode/battery.py`) run against original (via `git stash`) vs fixed code across all three touched scripts. Exactly 11 rows changed — all instances of the five regression classes — and every control (5-digit remarks, sub-rupee verifications, single-dash `CHQ PAID-`, mode-less IMPS, other NEFT/UPI/RTGS/cheque layouts, ordinary deposits) derived identically before and after.
